### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. developmental delay, hypotonia, musculoskeletal defects, and behavioral abnormalities  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:16974)

**Proposed mechanism:** SRCAP (HGNC:10739) —DISRUPTS→ Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006333); Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006333) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006333) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252); Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006333) —LEADS_TO→ Musculoskeletal defects (HP:0001198); Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006333) —LEADS_TO→ Behavioral abnormalities (HP:0000705); Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006333) —LEADS_TO→ Floating-Harbor syndrome (MONDO:0007621). Haploinsufficiency of SRCAP leads to disrupted chromatin remodeling, which in turn results in the developmental delay, hypotonia, musculoskeletal defects, and behavioral abnormalities characteristic of disease B, as well as the specific phenotype of Floating-Harbor syndrome (disease A).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in SRCAP with a gain-of-function mechanism in either disease, or the absence of any SRCAP variants in well-characterized cases of either disease. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of SRCAP in chromatin remodeling and its link to both Floating-Harbor syndrome and developmental delay, hypotonia, musculoskeletal defects, and behavioral abnormalities could lead to targeted therapies aimed at modulating chromatin structure for improved neurodevelopmental and physical outcomes.
